pivot: Whether the compressed research cycle gets routed through the liability/legal-exposure channel (courts, disclosure, regulators treating it as evidence of knowledge and control) or through the capability/safety-gating channel (thresholds, release-delay triggers) as the operative mechanism converting the compression into consequences
pivot_observable: The content of the first institutional response to a publicly attributable compressed research cycle — is it a disclosure/discovery order, liability-theory pleading, or AG/regulator inquiry citing 'knew and controlled' (liability channel), versus a threshold invocation, release-delay, or safety-review gate (capability channel)
pivot_because: Every minute agrees a compressed research cycle becomes publicly attributable and that this event matters, but they split hard on which downstream mechanism metabolizes it. pressure-model's move is the one that reorders the outcome set rather than shading confidence within it: if liability dominates, the observable evidence is legal filings, disclosure orders, and lab defensive positioning (lab-moves, ai-courts-decide, the revised ai-public-backlash and ai-rsi-timeline all converge here after round 2). If capability/threshold-gating dominates instead, the observable evidence is a lab invoking or dodging its own published trigger (ai-pressure's original frame) — a completely different set of institutions acts, on a different legal theory, with different remedies. That is a reordering, not a confidence shift, which is why four of six minutes revised toward pressure-model's frame between round 1 and round 2.
rival_pivots_rejected: ai-pressure's original pivot (does the lab honor or dodge its own published R&D-acceleration threshold) is a real question but sits downstream of the liability-vs-capability split — it's only decision-relevant if the capability/gating channel is the one doing the work, which is exactly what pressure-model contests and a majority came to agree it isn't. ai-courts-decide's pivot (court cycle-time vs. legislative cycle-time) is a real but narrower axis: it's a timing question inside the liability channel, not a question of which channel is operative, so it doesn't reorder the outcome set the way the liability/capability split does — it's a below-the-pivot elaboration, not the hinge itself.
ruling: The compressed research cycle will be absorbed primarily as evidence in the liability/disclosure fight (courts, AGs, lab defensive positioning) rather than triggering the capability-threshold/release-delay mechanism the brief's framework nominally specifies.
because: The round-2 revisions are the tell: ai-rsi-timeline and ai-public-backlash both explicitly abandoned their round-1 framing (regulatory/enforcement escalation via the safety-gating branch) to fold into pressure-model's liability-exposure mechanism, and lab-moves and ai-courts-decide's independently-argued claims (bargaining chip against compliance demands; discovery orders citing pace-of-change) are both liability-channel observables, not capability-gating ones. Only ai-pressure held the original capability-threshold framing, and its own round-2 defense concedes pressure-model's field displaces it rather than rebutting it on the merits.
threat_live: Newly live: legal/regulatory exposure from a lab's own compressed-research-cycle claim being read backward as proof it knew about and could have controlled capability gains it previously disclaimed as unpredictable — converting a capability-speed PR asset into a disclosure and knowledge liability. Newly dampened by the same branch: the safety-threshold/release-delay mechanism the brief's framework nominally offers, which every revised minute now expects to be routed around rather than invoked.
strongest_minute: pressure-model — it is the only minute whose mechanism (installed pressure converting from delay-flavored to disclosure-forcing branches) explains why four independent minutes converged onto it after round 1, rather than merely asserting a preferred outcome; it names the actual lever (courts/regulators reading capability as evidence of control) rather than just a date and a citation type.
weakest_minute: ai-pressure — its claim (labs quietly revise threshold language to avoid triggering it) treats the threshold-gating channel as still the operative mechanism, which is exactly the assumption the rest of the field abandoned by round 2; its round-2 DEFEND doesn't engage pressure-model's objection so much as restate the original claim.
shared_assumption: All six minutes assume the compressed-research-cycle claim, once made, is legible and attributable enough that outside institutions (courts, regulators, journalists) can act on it as a discrete fact rather than a contested or ambiguous metric — none argues about measurement validity or attribution difficulty itself.
smuggled_assumption: ai-courts-decide smuggles in a second assumption the brief didn't grant: that the relevant docket is specifically the fair-use/copyright track (OpenAI MDL) rather than a liability/disclosure track arising directly from the compression claim itself — the brief's branch is about the compression event's downstream effects generally, not about which existing docket absorbs it, and the round-2 minute doesn't defend why copyright litigation specifically is where compression-driven urgency lands.
unresolved: Whether a lab's disclosure-forcing exposure (pressure-model's liability channel) actually deters or delays capability releases in practice, or whether it runs in parallel with continued shipping — none of the minutes trace the liability branch through to an effect on release timing itself, only to a change in which institution reacts and on what theory.
